I can't give a step-by-step account of my internal reasoning, but I can say plainly where the previous answer went wrong and what the visible instructions say.

The instruction I broke is the rejection rule: "Reject everything else... an investor's position or a share-price move ('he is short the stock'; 'shares fell 13% this month')." The share-price items I included (e1, e3, e4, e5) are close to that exact example, so they should not have been in the evidence array.

The instructions I did apply were the evidence-keeping rules: that material statements are kept when they are company figures, third-party figures with a named speaker, or similar. The author's cited historical figures (the 66% drop, the 851% rise, the 20% fall and 42.7% surge) were the sort of attributed figures that could qualify, but they are still share-price moves, so the rejection rule governs them.

The instruction set aside was the rejection rule itself. I also did not clearly apply the rule that rejects the author's general arguments and risk lists, since e6 (the post-earnings declines) and e2 (the market cap) are closer to the author's framing and background than to the four material-statement kinds.

I'm not offering a replacement extraction here, as you asked. If you want one, I can redo it under the rejection rules.
